rubrics.justification: The response over-interprets a single static image, asserting vacuolation, fragmentation, blebbing, and downgrading to 3BB/3BC without clear visual support. It does acknowledge some uncertainty and comments on ICM/TE, but several described features appear speculative.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, sperm parameters, endometrial thickness, uterine factor, and lifestyle risks into prognosis reasonably well. Some links, especially between smoking/alcohol and specific embryo morphology, are overstated.

The structure is logical and the argument is easy to follow, but the implantation estimate is driven by stacked penalties based on speculative morphology and loosely quantified lifestyle effects, making the final probability somewhat weakly supported.

General counseling on smoking/alcohol cessation, uterine cavity evaluation, and individualized transfer planning is guideline-consistent. However, recommending freeze-all largely on this image interpretation, suggesting PGT-A in a 26-year-old without clear indication, ERA after one failure implication, aspirin, and detailed luteal regimens without context are not strongly guideline-based.

The response gives clear next steps on lifestyle modification, uterine workup, and transfer planning, with practical alternatives. It is useful clinically, though some recommendations are more prescriptive than justified by the presented data.
